note.text:
Solve an inequality like an equation, doing the same thing to both sides:
• Adding or subtracting the same number keeps the sign: x + 3 < 7 gives x < 4.
• Multiplying or dividing by a positive number keeps the sign: 2x ≥ 10 gives x ≥ 5.
• Multiplying or dividing by a negative number turns the sign round: −3x < 6 gives x > −2. (Check: x = 0 works, because −3 × 0 = 0 < 6.)
Two steps: 2x + 1 > 9. Subtract 1: 2x > 8. Divide by 2: x > 4.
The whole-number solutions can be listed: if x < 4 and x is a natural number, x can be 0, 1, 2 or 3.

worked_example.problem: Solve {poly([a, 'x'], [b, ''])} ≤ {c}, then list the natural numbers that satisfy it.
steps: Divide both sides by {a}, a positive number, so the sign stays: x ≤ {(c - b) / a}.
The natural numbers that are less than or equal to {(c - b) / a}: {solutionsIn(0, (c - b) / a, '≤', (c - b) / a)}.
worked_example.answer: x ≤ {(c - b) / a}: x = {solutionsIn(0, (c - b) / a, '≤', (c - b) / a)}

cards.idea: Adding or subtracting the same number on both sides keeps the inequality sign.
Dividing both sides by a positive number keeps the sign.
Dividing both sides by a negative number turns the sign round.
example: {mono(a, 'x')} < {a * k}: divide by {br(a)} and turn the sign: x > {k}.
Check with x = {k + one}: {a} × {br(k + one)} = {a * (k + one)}, which is less than {a * k}.

misconceptions.explain: You divided by a negative number, {br(a)}: the sign must turn round.
{a * k} ÷ {br(a)} = {k}: check the sign of the number.

solution: Divide both sides by {br(a)}, a negative number, so the sign turns round.

cards.idea: The whole-number solutions of an inequality can be listed.
example: x < {k} with x a natural number: x = {solutionsIn(0, k, '<', k)}.

Those are the values on the other side of {k}.

questions.prompt: What is the largest whole number x such that {poly([a, 'x'], [b, ''])} < {c}?

misconceptions.explain: x must be less than {(c - b) / a}, so x cannot be {(c - b) / a} itself.
x must be less than {round((c - b) / a, 2)}: round down.

solution: {b < 0 ? 'Add ' + fmt(-b) + ' to' : 'Subtract ' + fmt(b) + ' from'} both sides: {mono(a, 'x')} < {c - b}.
The largest whole number less than {(c - b) / a} is {answer}.
